purpose: Frozen blind set measured once per system, never used for tuning. Scope: source-heldout (FT answer passages excluded), not unseen-evidence (FT context overlap allowed). Curated from the frozen corpus without running any retriever or model. Part a uses only odd letter years.

cases.query: Why does Buffett say the restrictions Berkshire places on its big blocks of stock actually benefit the company's owners and the managers involved?

gold_claims.claim: The restrictions leave the long-term economic prospects of these businesses enhanced by the arrangements, because first-class managers can focus on running the businesses.
gold_claims.verification_note: 1985 letter; unit=qualitative economic rationale; definition=why block restrictions help owners, not a price claim.

gold_claims.claim: Because corporate instability is an inevitable consequence of widely-diffused ownership, circumscribing the blocks helps promote stability.
gold_claims.verification_note: 1985 letter; unit=qualitative governance rationale; definition=stability benefit of limiting block sales.

gold_claims.claim: The managers are assured there will be no surprises, and the agreements give them a corporate commitment even if Buffett's participation ends prematurely.
gold_claims.verification_note: 1985 letter; unit=qualitative human rationale; definition=assurance given to managers.

cases.verification_note: 1985_p0128-0130 give the economic, stability and human reasons for restricting Berkshire's large blocks.

cases.query: Why does Buffett treat insurance as a commodity business, and what edge does Berkshire say it has over competitors?

gold_claims.claim: Even commodity businesses flourish when shortages exist, yet insurance managers rushed to expand capacity as they did in 1985-87.
gold_claims.verification_note: 1987 letter; unit=qualitative industry cycle; definition=commodity pricing power only in shortages.

gold_claims.claim: Berkshire works to escape commodity economics by trying to differentiate our product with financial strength that exceeds all others in the industry.
gold_claims.verification_note: 1987 letter; unit=qualitative competitive strategy; definition=differentiation through financial strength.

gold_claims.claim: When buyers focus on insurers with enduring financial strength, Berkshire will lead the pack.
gold_claims.verification_note: 1987 letter; unit=qualitative competitive advantage; definition=advantage when buyers focus on claim-paying ability.

cases.verification_note: 1987_p0046-0048 describe shortage-driven commodity economics and Berkshire's financial-strength edge.
